objects.title: Analysis: the pace of work on reporting thresholds for small remittance and cross-border payment transactions
objects.rawText: Capital Policy Times analysis: work on reporting thresholds for small remittance and cross-border payment transactions is moving faster than expected, according to people close to Finance, Economy and Planning Committee. The related bill is "Act Partially Amending the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Annual Limit for Small Remittance Providers)" (22-S0497).

objects.title: Ryu Taehwan calls for wider consultation on a pedestrian priority rule for outdoor mobile robots
objects.rawText: Ryu Taehwan (Party A) released a statement on a pedestrian priority rule for outdoor mobile robots and called for wider consultation before a vote. The related bill is "Act Partially Amending the Road Traffic Act (Cargo-Class Robots and Operator Duties on Sidewalks)" (22-S0308).

objects.title: Analysis: the pace of work on the novel food ingredient approval process for cultivated protein
objects.rawText: Metro Business Review analysis: work on the novel food ingredient approval process for cultivated protein is moving faster than expected, according to people close to Ministry of Food and Drug Safety.

objects.title: Yun Gaon calls for wider consultation on operator liability and insurance coverage after robot accidents
objects.rawText: Yun Gaon (Party A) released a statement on operator liability and insurance coverage after robot accidents and called for wider consultation before a vote. The related bill is "Act Partially Amending the Intelligent Robots Act (Minimum Insurance Coverage by Weight Class)" (22-S0357).

objects.title: Consultation notice on conditions for overseas transfer of personal information

Written comments are accepted for the period stated in the notice. The related bill is "Act Partially Amending the Personal Information Protection Act (Overseas Transfer Conditions)" (22-S0511).

objects.title: Issue brief: sidewalk rules for outdoor mobile robots
objects.body:
# Issue brief: sidewalk rules for outdoor mobile robots

## Situation

Since November 2023, certified outdoor mobile robots of up to 500 kg and 15 km/h count as pedestrians and may use sidewalks. The sidewalk robot duties bill (22-S0308) passed the Public Administration and Security bill review subcommittee on Nov 12 and goes to the full committee on Nov 19.

## Client position

Aster Robotics backs sidewalk access for cargo-class robots and wants the stop rule replaced by a duty to slow to walking pace and give way.

## What changes

The subcommittee text lets cargo-class robots up to 1,000 mm wide use sidewalks at least 3 m wide, but makes them stop for any pedestrian within 2 m. On narrower sidewalks that would stall most of Aster Robotics' city routes.

## Next steps

We ask Baek Siwoo, the lead sponsor, to carry the slow-and-yield wording at the full committee on Nov 19, brief the subcommittee chair on the same wording, and tell the committee chair's office when the vote is expected. The industry forum is drafting a joint amendment that we will share with the sponsor and the subcommittee chair.

objects.title: Draft comments on the sidewalk operation standards notice
objects.body:
# Comments on the sidewalk operation standards notice

To the Traffic Safety Division, Korean National Police Agency

Aster Robotics welcomes the government bill on sidewalk operation standards for outdoor mobile robots, open for comment until Dec 7. Standards set by robot class in the enforcement decree will let operators and police apply the same rules on every sidewalk.

We ask that the enforcement decree the bill authorizes add a cargo class for certified robots up to 1,000 mm wide, with a duty to slow to walking pace and give way to pedestrians rather than to stop. Our pilot route logs show that robots meeting this duty keep sidewalks moving while protecting pedestrians.

We also ask that robots running inside a designated pilot zone be exempt in the decree from the width and speed limits for the length of the pilot, so cities can test new routes before national rules change. We would welcome the chance to share our route data with the Division.

objects.body:
# Issue brief: prepaid balance safeguarding

## Situation

The Financial Services Commission has put a government bill on prepaid balance safeguarding out for legislative notice. Comments close on Nov 27. The commission must consider them but is not bound, and the text can still change in regulatory review, the Ministry of Government Legislation and the Cabinet before the bill reaches the National Assembly, usually months later.

## Client position

Wrenfield Pay already keeps prepaid funds in a segregated trust account and has no position on the bill until the final standard is known.

## What changes

The bill would require every prepaid issuer to hold customer funds apart from operating funds, through a trust account or a payment guarantee.

## Next steps

We file comments by Nov 26 asking that existing trust accounts count as compliant, and send the supervisory service the fund segregation procedure once Wrenfield Pay provides it.

objects.title: Stop rule for pedestrians
objects.summary: The subcommittee text makes robots stop for any pedestrian within 2 m. On sidewalks under 3 m wide that would stall most of Aster Robotics' city routes.

objects.title: A single certification body
objects.summary: The government bill would move certification to one designated body. New models could wait months for a certificate.

objects.title: Cargo class in the enforcement decree
objects.summary: The police agency notice is open for comment. The bill leaves robot classes and operation standards to an enforcement decree, so comments can ask that the decree include a cargo class and pilot zone exemptions. The bill amends the same article as the sidewalk robot duties bill, so the committee may fold the two together once it is submitted.

objects.title: Joint amendment with the industry forum
objects.summary: Other operators back the same slow-and-yield wording. A joint text carries more weight with the committee.

objects.title: Ban on meat terms

objects.title: Local presence requirement
objects.summary: The bill would require a local office before registration, which would delay launch. The subcommittee reviews it together with the capital requirement bill, which amends the same articles, so one combined text leaves the subcommittee.

objects.desiredOutcome: Aster Robotics runs cargo models on city sidewalks next year under a yield rule its robots already meet.
messages: Pilot route logs show robots already slow to walking pace near pedestrians.
A robot that stops dead on a narrow sidewalk blocks people longer than one that slows and moves aside.
Cargo-class robots carry the pharmacy and grocery orders small shops cannot send by motorbike.

objects.desiredOutcome: One national certification path with recognized test bodies, in force before the next model launch.
messages: City-by-city rules would mean testing the same robot several times.
Recognizing existing test bodies avoids a certification backlog.

objects.desiredOutcome: Mandatory insurance with minimum coverage scaled by robot weight.
messages: Coverage should scale with weight and speed, as it does for other machines.
A flat minimum prices small operators out of the market.

objects.desiredOutcome: Cities can designate robot pilot zones, and more cities join next year.
messages: Pilot zones let cities test before national rules change.
Aster Robotics can commit routes in three cities once zones are approved.

objects.desiredOutcome: A statutory review deadline for novel ingredients written into the committee alternative.
messages: Without a deadline, review can take years and investment goes abroad.
Other markets set fixed review periods with the same safety bar.

objects.desiredOutcome: Descriptive terms such as "cultivated meat" stay allowed with a clear origin label.
messages: Consumers understand descriptive terms when the origin is on the front label.
Research on label comprehension shows the origin line matters more than the noun.

objects.desiredOutcome: A food-tech sandbox with time-limited sales permits while review is pending.
messages: Supervised sales build the safety record regulators ask for.
Permits should carry a review deadline so they do not lapse.

objects.desiredOutcome: Wrenfield Pay registers and launches next year without opening a local office.
messages: A local agent gives regulators the same reach as a local office.
A presence rule delays entry and keeps fees high for users.

objects.desiredOutcome: Segregation rules that accept trust accounts already in use.
messages: Customer funds held in a segregated trust account are protected the same way.
Rules should accept trust accounts and payment guarantees alike.

objects.desiredOutcome: A higher annual remittance limit with a simple reporting path.
messages: Higher limits let migrant workers send money home at lower cost.
Automatic reporting gives the ministry the same data without a filing per transfer.

objects.desiredOutcome: Standard contract clauses recognized as a lawful transfer route.
messages: Standard clauses protect data abroad without forcing local servers.
Clear clauses make supervision easier for the commission.
